source.title: DyGen: Learning from Noisy Labels via Dynamics-Enhanced Generative Modeling
source.authors: Yu-Chen Zhuang; Yue Yu; Lingkai Kong; Xiang Chen; Chao Zhang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Reports its own training-dynamics measurements bearing on learning clean patterns before fitting noisy labels, using language-model fine-tuning and embedding-distance measures rather than the original image-network experiments.
record.gate_note: The study measures embedding dynamics during fine-tuning with corrupted labels. Its benchmark accuracy results do not measure training error on random labels, time to fit them, unstructured inputs, regularization effects, or test error approaching chance. It also does not compare learning real labels with learning fully random labels.
record.test_reason: The study uses an early-learning/memorization interpretation to develop a denoising method. Its own observations measure embedding geometry, not when clean and noisy labels are fitted. Early true-label clustering can reflect pretrained semantic knowledge, as §4.1 acknowledges. Neither the embedding statistics nor the method's test accuracy establishes V6's learning order.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the observed embedding differences and movement. The authors interpret these patterns as likely arising from clean-pattern learning followed by noise memorization; that mechanism is an interpretation rather than a directly measured learning order. Their main conclusion is that these dynamics improve denoising through DyGen.
record.recipe_differences: Measures embedding distances and visualized trajectories during PLM fine-tuning on text datasets with synthetic or weak-label noise; it does not reproduce the original image-network random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported settings include different PLMs, datasets, and noise types and ratios; the paper states the pattern occurs consistently across its experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Noisy samples have larger mean and standard deviation of distances to assigned-label centroids across fine-tuning epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Embedding-distance statistics distinguish clean and noisy training examples during PLM fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected noisy examples move from true-label clusters toward assigned-label clusters between early and late fine-tuning visualizations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noisy-label fine-tuning changes pretrained representations toward the assigned noisy classes.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 29th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD ’23)
record.problems: The evidence relevant to V6 is qualitative for the embedding-distance pattern, with example visualizations and no reported uncertainty for that measure. The study does not compare fully random labels against real labels.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error and chance test performance under completely random labeling with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true and random labels, and convergence slowdown as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit throughout increasing corruption and steady test-error degradation from no corruption to completely random labels. Reported clean-test accuracy curves do not establish this joint behavior.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and of removing them on true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of actual clean-pattern fitting and noisy-label memorization, and direct comparison of real-label and random-label learning trajectories.

record.verdict_notes: The corrected states concern whether each measure establishes a claim version; they do not dispute the reported embedding observations. The hypothesized requirement that systematic bias not dominate clean signal is not an experimentally demonstrated scope limit.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard deep networks fit completely random image labels with near-zero training error and chance test error, without changing architecture or hyperparameters.
Training time to fit random labels and how convergence time changes with corrupted-label fraction.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Whether training error remains perfect and test error rises steadily across corruption levels while signal is retained.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent fitting random labels, and whether their removal harms generalization on true labels.
The study examines noisy labels in text classification, not fully random labels or image networks; it does not directly compare the learning trajectories for real versus random labels.

rows.subject: various PLMs, including BERT, BioBERT, PubMedBERT, and RoBERTa
rows.operation_detail: Compared mean and standard deviation of embedding distances to assigned-label cluster centroids for clean and noisy samples during training.

conditions.value: 20newsgroup, AG News, ChemProt, TREC, and SemEval
synthetic and real-world noise at various ratios

rows.measure: Mean and standard deviation of distances to assigned-label cluster centroids over training epochs
rows.baseline: Clean samples exhibited smaller mean and deviation of distances
rows.value: Noisy samples consistently exhibited a higher mean and deviation in distances
rows.note: Qualitative aggregate result across the stated trials; the paper does not provide a per-model breakdown for this aggregate claim.
rows.check: Larger mean and standard deviation of embedding distances distinguish noisy from clean samples but do not establish which labels are learned first. Statistics aggregated across epochs do not establish temporal order.

rows.subject: BERT-base
rows.operation_detail: Visualized training embeddings of clean and corrupted samples at early and late fine-tuning stages.
rows.measure: Sample positions relative to true-label and assigned-label clusters over training
rows.baseline: Early-stage embeddings: samples remained closer to their true-label clusters
rows.value: Black points representing noisy samples moved from the true-label cluster to the assigned-label cluster during fine-tuning
rows.note: The paper describes this as an example visualization.
rows.check: The reported embedding movement is accurately described, but the epoch-2 and epoch-10 visualizations do not measure clean-pattern fitting followed by noisy-label memorization. Initial clustering can reflect pretraining. Figure 2 also displays only five selected categories.
